title: Adding on an Open Number Line

steps.body: An open number line trades the column for a journey: start at one number and jump — hundreds first, then tens, then ones.
steps.narration: An open number line trades the column for a journey: start at one number and jump — hundreds first, then tens, then ones.

widget.prompt: Add 200 to 347 on the open line: hop by hundreds.

commonLandings.feedback: Those hops moved by TENS. A hundred-jump slides the leftmost digit: 347 → 447 → 547.
That is one hundred-jump. Adding 200 takes two of them.

widget.missFeedback: Each hop is 100. From 347, 2 hops land on 547.
widget.successFeedback: 547 — two hundred-jumps, and the hundreds digit is the only one that moved.

predict.prompt: Starting at 347 and adding 200, which digit changes?
predict.reveal: Adding whole hundreds leaves the tens and ones untouched — 347 becomes 547 with 4 and 7 standing still.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and watch what each trade does to g3a open line.
invariants: A trade never changes how much there is — ten ones become one ten, one hundred becomes ten tens, and the total stands still while the packaging changes for g3a open line.
misconceptions: Flipping a column to take the small digit from the large one, stranding a carry, or borrowing from a column that has nothing to lend.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If a column comes up short, what must change somewhere else so the total stays exactly the same?

widget.prompt: What is one hundred more than 282?

commonErrors.feedback: That added one TEN. A hundred more moves the hundreds digit, not the tens.
That added one ONE — the smallest place, when the question named the largest.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Work one place at a time, and trade only when a column truly comes up short.

widget.prompt: On an open number line you start at 347 and want to add 200. Which jump set is most efficient?

options.label: Two jumps of 100
options.feedback: Correct — 200 is exactly two hundred-jumps: 347 → 447 → 547, and the line stays readable.

options.label: Twenty jumps of 10
options.feedback: It lands correctly but draws twenty hops where two will do — the open line rewards big jumps first.

options.label: Two hundred jumps of 1
options.feedback: That is counting by ones with extra steps; the open line exists to escape exactly that.

options.label: One jump of 100
options.feedback: One hundred-jump adds only 100, stopping halfway to the 200 you were asked to add.
